lawRefs: ESSB 5813, Laws of 2025 ch. 421 (tiered capital gains rate from tax year 2025)
SB 6346 (2026) (9.9% income tax on income over $1 million, effective Jan 1 2028)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Values hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Washington DOR: "Washington does not currently have an individual income tax." No tax on wages, interest, dividends, pensions or Social Security in 2026, so kind is "none". NOT EXPRESSIBLE IN THIS SCHEMA: Washington levies a capital gains EXCISE tax (RCW 82.87) on net long-term capital gains allocated to Washington: 7% on the first $1,000,000 of taxable gains and 9.9% (7% plus an additional 2.9%) on the excess (tiered from tax year 2025), after an annual standard deduction per individual OR per married couple/domestic partnership (not doubled for couples): $270,000 for 2024 and $278,000 for 2025. The deduction is inflation-adjusted annually and the 2026 amount had not been published by DOR on the retrieval date. Real estate, assets held in retirement accounts and several other asset classes are exempt; a charitable deduction applies above a floor (capped at $111,000 in 2025). Future law: SB 6346 (signed March 30, 2026) imposes a 9.9% income tax on adjusted gross income above $1 million beginning January 1, 2028 (first returns due 2029); it does not apply to 2026. The WA Cares payroll premium (0.58% of wages) is also outside this schema. Cross-checked against Tax Foundation, "State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets, 2026" (data as of Jan 1 2026, updated Feb 11 2026).

flags.longTermGainExclusionPct: not applicable: no income tax, but a separate 7% / 9.9% capital-gains excise applies above an annual standard deduction (2025: $278,000; 2026 amount not yet published) - see notes; the engine needs a separate rule for it
